title: K-Means vs Gaussian Mixture Models
question: Does a soft, flexible-shape model (GMM) find stable groups where K-Means did not?
methodology: GMM, full covariance, n_init=5, on fully evolved / relative stats (HP share dropped: shares sum to 1). Same pre-registered rule as K-Means; BIC to choose among eligible k.
interpretation: GMM also has no eligible k and is less stable than K-Means at every k=3-8 (GMM ARI 0.36-0.46). BIC is lowest at k=4, but that k is unstable. GMM reports high confidence (mean top probability 0.83-0.89) while its groups change across resamples: model probabilities assume the model is right and do not measure stability.
limitations: Silhouette favors round groups, so it penalizes GMM's stretched groups by design; bootstrap stability is the fairer comparison and also fails.
